newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sino Land rises on warrant rumours.
newsitem.headline: Sino Land rises on warrant rumours.

text.p: Shares of property group Sino Land Co Ltd rose late Wednesday morning on buying fueled by rumours of a possible issue of warrants on the stock after the company reported its yearly profit on Tuesday, brokers said.

"Speculation that the warrant issuer might need to buy stock to cover the warrants boosted buying, particularly after it reported an encouraging yearly earnings growth," said a dealing director at a local brokerage.
Sino shares rose HK$0.05 to HK$8.50 at midday on volume of 6.27 million shares worth HK$53.12 million.
Brokers said it was rumoured that a merchant bank was planning to issue 280 million warrants, carrying a premium of 13 percent and a gearing of 4.3 times, on shares of Sino Land.

Analysts said Sino Land's 60 percent drop in 1995/96 net profit to HK$1.15 billion was in line with expectations, because the company actually achieved earnings growth of 21 percent if excluded an exceptional gain of HK$1.92 billion in the 1994/95 fiscal year.
